<explanation>
Based on our analysis of the file tree and README, HippoRAG 2 is a research-driven framework focused on giving large language models (LLMs) enhanced “memory” capabilities by integrating retrieval augmented generation (RAG) with continual learning techniques. The project is modular, handling tasks such as embedding generation, information extraction, LLM inference, prompt management, and evaluation—all integrated under one cohesive system. Below is a step-by-step explanation for drawing a system design diagram that accurately represents this architecture.

1. Identify the Main Components
   • HippoRAG Core: Represented by the main orchestrator (HippoRAG.py) which coordinates indexing, retrieval, and question answering.
   • Embedding Model Module: Under src/hipporag/embedding_model, this module provides different embedding models (NV-Embed-v2, GritLM, Contriever, OpenAIEmbedding) for transforming text into vector representations.
   • LLM Inference Module: Found in src/hipporag/llm, this handles LLM queries with support for both OpenAI models and local deployments (vLLM). Include both online and offline variants.
   • Information Extraction Module: In src/hipporag/information_extraction, it handles Open Information Extraction (OpenIE) for processing text, implemented for both online (OpenAI) and offline (vLLM) scenarios.
   • Prompt Management: Under src/hipporag/prompts, this module manages various prompt templates (including filtering and linking prompts) to be fed to LLMs.
   • Evaluation Module: Located in src/hipporag/evaluation, this part provides evaluation metrics and logic for both QA and retrieval assessments.
   • Utilities and Configurations: Under src/hipporag/utils, these cover logging, configuration management, and miscellaneous helper functions.
   • Data Storage & Outputs: The repository contains directories like outputs (storing generated results), reproduce (with datasets and experiment support), and main/demonstration scripts (demo.py, main.py).

2. Show Relationships and Data Flow
   • Begin with the Data Input/Corpus: Start by showing the ingestion of textual data or corpus from dataset files (e.g., in reproduce/dataset) and how it flows into a pre-processing stage.
   • Embedding Generation: Indicate that documents are passed into the embedding model module, which transforms passages into embeddings.
   • Indexing & Storage: Once embeddings are created, they are managed and stored via the embedding_store (a dedicated component for saving and managing embeddings).
   • Retrieval & Information Extraction: When queries are made, the system goes through retrieval:
       – The retrieval module uses the embedding store to find relevant passages in a multi-hop manner.
       – In parallel, the information extraction module (using OpenIE) may extract factual candidates and entities that inform the retrieval process.
   • LLM Integration for QA: After retrieving relevant passages, these outputs are forwarded to the LLM module where the appropriate language model (either via OpenAI API or local vLLM) generates answers. Include a branch that shows both direct QA (combined retrieval & QA) and separate steps for retrieval then QA.
   • Prompt Management: Illustrate that before reaching the LLM, the prompt_template_manager integrates appropriate prompt templates (from src/hipporag/prompts) to tailor the questions or instructions passed to the LLM.
   • Evaluation: Finally, depict how the outputs are compared against expected answers using the Evaluation module to compute retrieval and QA metrics.
   
   Use directional arrows between each component to show this flow—from data ingestion, through embedding conversion, indexing, retrieval, prompt management, LLM inference, and finally to evaluation or result output.

3. Highlight Architectural Patterns and Technologies
   • Separation of Concerns: Each module (embedding, LLM, information extraction, evaluation) is self-contained, making it straightforward to swap or update individual components.
   • Modularity and Extensibility: Given the multiple models supported (several embedding models and LLM frameworks) and the prompt management system, the design is clearly built for extensibility.
   • Hybrid Deployment Support: The system diagram should show that the LLM module has two deployment paths: external API (OpenAI) and local server (vLLM), ensuring the diagram reflects decision points based on runtime configuration.
   • Experimental Infrastructure: Indicate additional support for reproducibility (reproduce folder, dataset management) and output logging (outputs directory).

4. Tailoring the Diagram to HippoRAG 2’s Purpose
   • Emphasize the dual role of RAG—retrieval and question answering—with continual learning elements (memory aspect) to connect and update knowledge.
   • Clearly showcase how the embedding generation, retrieval, and extraction components work together to enable more associative and contextually rich responses.
   • Include technologies such as OpenAI GPT models, meta-llama/Llama (via vLLM), and various text embedding models. Also note dependencies like Huggingface and conda environments as part of the deployment context (these can be annotated).
   • Use color coding or distinct shapes: for example, use one color for model-related components (LLM, embedding models), another for core orchestration (HippoRAG core), and another for utility and support modules (evaluation, prompts, config).

5. Diagram Layout Guidelines for the Principal Software Engineer
   • Use clear labels for each major component (e.g., “HippoRAG Core”, “Embedding Model”, “LLM Inference”, “Information Extraction”, “Prompt Manager”, “Evaluation”).
   • Draw directional arrows that indicate data or process flow (e.g., “Data Ingestion” → “Embedding Generation” → “Indexing” → “Retrieval” → “LLM QA”).
   • Include annotations for deployment choices (e.g., separate arrows or branches indicating “OpenAI API” vs. “Local vLLM Server”).
   • Different shapes (e.g., rectangles for modules, cylinders for data storage) and color coding (e.g., blue for computational modules, green for storage components) improve clarity.
   • Aim for high detail: Include critical configuration files (setup.py, requirements.txt) in a “Deployment & Setup” section if desired, so that integration or environment orchestration is visible.
   • Optionally, include a “Workflow” arrow that represents the recursive nature of continual learning (i.e., updating memory/knowledge graphs after each QA session).

By following these guidelines, the resulting diagram will not only show an accurate breakdown of HippoRAG 2’s architecture but will also highlight the key interactions, deployment alternatives, and the modular nature of the system. This detailed, component-wise diagram will serve as both an overview and a reference for understanding and potentially extending the project’s capabilities.
</explanation>
